# Verstappen seals commanding Singapore Grand Prix victory from Leclerc and Antonelli
Red Bull's Max Verstappen continued his winning form by triumphing in the Singapore Grand Prix on his 250th Grand Prix start.
Oct 11, 2026 2:06pm UTC
Max Verstappen put in an assured drive to take victory in the Singapore Grand Prix, the Red Bull driver holding the lead throughout the hot and humid encounter to seal his first-ever Grand Prix win at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.
After defending against Charles Leclerc into the first corner, Verstappen ensured that he emerged in P1 and, while the Ferrari initially remained on his tail, the four-time World Champion soon built up a significant gap at the front.
The mid-race pit stops phase did little to change Verstappen’s commanding run, the Dutchman enjoying a smooth stop as he switched from the soft to the medium tyres.
From there onwards he was untroubled at the front and, despite suffering some radio issues that resulted in the team having to use the pit board for communication, Verstappen ultimately clinched his 73rd career win on his 250th Grand Prix start.
Leclerc held onto P2, crossing the line 7.3 seconds behind, while Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli completed the podium in third – a result that would extend the youngster’s championship lead further.
The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri were fourth and fifth, ahead of the other Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton. Liam Lawson claimed P7 to add to Racing Bulls’ tally, with Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg just behind in eighth.

Fernando Alonso brought his Aston Martin home in P16, followed by Cadillac’s Sergio Perez. Alex Albon was classified as P18 for Williams despite retiring in the closing stages, while the other Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas rounded out the order in P19.
Three drivers retired from the event, with Aston Martin’s Lance Stroll suffering a suspected clutch issue, Alpine’s Franco Colapinto experiencing a driveline problem and Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto experiencing what appeared to be a gearbox problem.
### AS IT HAPPENED
The first two days on track at the Marina Bay Street Circuit had already proven to be action-packed, with Verstappen emerging as the winner of a dramatic, rain-affected Sprint before securing pole position – his first at this venue – a few hours later in Qualifying.
But now it was time for the main event, as the attentions of the paddock turned to the 62-lap Singapore Grand Prix. Hot and humid conditions were again in force as the drivers started their preparations for the event, while some would perhaps breathe a sigh of relief that no further rain had arrived as of yet.
It was confirmed in the build-up to the race that a few alterations had been made to the starting order, with Russell dropping back to P19 due to an engine penalty. ## F1 – Verstappen takes commanding Singapore victory ahead of Leclerc and Antonelli

 11.10.26 

Max Verstappen took his first Singapore Grand Prix victory with a controlled drive at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, beating Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc by 7.335 seconds as championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed third following a late battle for the final podium place.

The Red Bull driver led throughout the 62-lap race to secure his 73rd career victory, managing a one-stop strategy through two Virtual Safety Car periods. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finished fourth and fifth for McLaren, ahead of Lewis Hamilton, whose attempt to complete the race without a second stop left him vulnerable in the closing stages.

At the start, Leclerc made a strong getaway from second, but Verstappen moved across to protect the inside and retained the lead into Turn 1. Hamilton held third ahead of Antonelli, while Norris and Piastri avoided further contact after their collision in the Sprint.

Further back, Liam Lawson moved into seventh and Nico Hülkenberg and Carlos Sainz gained places to run eighth and 10th respectively. Oliver Bearman emerged ahead of Haas team-mate Esteban Ocon after an early scrap, while George Russell began his recovery from the back of the grid, reaching 15th by lap five.

Leclerc initially stayed within range of Verstappen, running six tenths behind and able to use Overtake Mode. The leader gradually eased away, however, as the opening stint developed.

The first interruption came when Gabriel Bortoleto stopped near the pit lane exit with an apparent gearbox problem. A Virtual Safety Car allowed his Audi to be recovered, before a subsequent fire required marshals to extinguish the flames and prompted a brief closure of the pit lane entry.

Once racing resumed, Verstappen continued to set the pace. By lap 15 his advantage had grown to 2.6 seconds, while Hamilton, starting on medium tyres, was coming under pressure from Antonelli and the McLarens.

Ferrari brought Hamilton in on lap 19 for soft tyres, sending him back out seventh behind Lawson. He passed the Racing Bulls driver on lap 21, but the early stop left Ferrari considering whether another visit would be required before the finish.

Antonelli stopped for mediums on lap 24, with Leclerc following one lap later. The Monegasque rejoined narrowly ahead of Hamilton, who reported losing time behind his team-mate despite running the softer compound.

Verstappen extended his opening stint, holding a 17.9-second advantage over Norris by lap 28 as Piastri ran third. Behind them, Russell continued to progress, passing Ocon at Turn 16 and gaining further positions as others stopped.

Alpine lost Franco Colapinto to a suspected gearbox problem, while Hülkenberg’s pit stop helped Russell climb to ninth. Antonelli, meanwhile, reported fluid leaking around his feet, adding another concern to a race in which he had already received warnings for exceeding track limits.

Verstappen finally stopped on lap 33, switching to medium tyres and retaining the lead. Norris followed and emerged behind Antonelli, before a slower stop for Piastri left the Australian six seconds behind his team-mate in sixth.

With the leading stops completed, attention shifted to tyre endurance and the contrasting strategies at Ferrari. Hamilton remained behind Leclerc, while Antonelli received a black and white flag for track limits and asked Mercedes to investigate unusual behaviour from his car.

A second Virtual Safety Car followed when Lance Stroll stopped at Turn 15 with a clutch issue. Leclerc and Antonelli used the interruption to make their second stops, while Russell came in for his first as the neutralisation ended, reducing the benefit available to the Mercedes driver.

Singapore Grand Prix result: Max Verstappen wins from Charles Leclerc with Kimi Antonelli third - BBC Sport
# Verstappen dominates for first grand prix win in Singapore
Image source, PA Media
Image caption, Before this weekend, Max Verstappen had not won a race in Singapore
By
Andrew Benson
F1 Correspondent in Singapore
11 October 2026, 14:54 BST
Updated 7 minutes ago
**Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second dominant victory within a week as he secured his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix.**
Verstappen fought off an attack from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc off the start line to control the race from start to finish.
The win followed his and Red Bull's maiden victory of the year in Malaysia last weekend and confirms the team's re-emergence as a major force.
Leclerc took second as team-mate Lewis Hamilton finished sixth after a baffling strategy from his team.
Hamilton, trying to last out on a set of soft tyres for a mammoth 44 laps, lost out in the closing laps to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Antonelli's third place combined with team-mate George Russell finishing only ninth after starting from 19th extends the Italian's championship lead to 102 points.
That means it is possible for Antonelli to clinch his first world title at the next race, the United States Grand Prix on 25 October.
He would need to win the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower to become champion in Austin.
The key stories of the race were:
* Verstappen's dominance reviving memories of his pomp during his title-winning era
* A confusing day at Ferrari with regard to strategy
* Antonelli closing on the world title
Verstappen knew he needed to get into the first corner first to try to win the race, given the difficulty of overtaking in Singapore and he fought tooth and nail to make sure he did.
Leclerc got a better start than Verstappen off the line and challenged down the inside as they approached Turn One.
But Verstappen squeezed him tight towards the pit wall and with their entry to the first corner so compromised, Leclerc eventually backed off and the four-time champion could claim the corner.
Verstappen, Leclerc and Hamilton ran nose to tail for the first four laps before the seven-time champion began to drop back from about lap five.
Leclerc stuck within a second of Verstappen for a further five laps before the Red Bull began to edge away from him as well.
From then on, Verstappen continued to build his lead and never looked like being beaten as he motored away into the distance.
Hamilton had started on the medium tyres while Verstappen and Leclerc chose the softs. Despite his theoretically more durable tyres, the Briton pitted on lap 18 to switch to the softs, while Leclerc waited until lap 24 to swap his softs for mediums.
Leclerc came out of the pits from his stop just ahead of Hamilton, who had stronger pace on his softer tyres.
Yet Ferrari chose not to order Leclerc to let Hamilton through to maximise his pace, a decision that was questioned by Hamilton from the car.
A virtual safety car was called on lap 39 and Leclerc and Antonelli, who had chased the Ferraris closely from the start from his fourth place on the grid, took the opportunity for a cheap pit stop - it takes 10 seconds less to stop under a safety car than under racing conditions.
Yet Hamilton, despite having older tyres, did not stop, a decision that promoted him to second behind Verstappen.
As Leclerc was catching Hamilton, the Briton was told he needed to stop again; he pushed back to suggest he try to go to the end, but was told they were six laps short to make it in terms of tyre life.
Leclerc soon caught Hamilton and passed him on lap 46 and set off after Verstappen, but could get no closer than 7.3 seconds to the Red Bull.

## Max masters Marina Bay at last as Isack battles to a point

Max Verstappen celebrated his 250th F1 Grand Prix with a commanding lights-to-flag maiden win in Singapore. The Dutchman dominated a punishing evening at the Marina Bay Street Circuit to finish seven seconds clear of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, with Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli third. Isack Hadjar, meanwhile, delivered a gritty performance to climb from a pit lane start to 10th and claim a point.

Max masters Marina Bay at last as Isack battles to a point© Getty Images

> 
> Max Verstappen

“We had pace when we needed to have it on the Soft tyre and on the Medium, even though I think the Medium tyre for everyone was a bit more of a struggle. But it worked out, so of course very happy to win here.” said Max of victory at a track where he had previously scored four podiums but no wins.

After recovering from a poor getaway to win yesterday’s Sprint, Max had said there was work to do overnight. When the lights went out for the Grand Prix, his and the Team’s efforts were rewarded. Max initially got away slowly, but a strong second phase allowed him to fend off Charles and lead out of Turn 1. 

At the other end of the order, Isack started from the pit lane on Medium tyres and moved into P20 behind Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso as the race got under way. 

Having converted pole into the lead, Max immediately got his head down and set about breaking out of Charles’ overtake mode range. On lap 7, he set the fastest lap of the race to move 1.2 seconds clear of the Ferrari driver, with Lewis Hamilton another 1.6 seconds back in third, ahead of Kimi and Lando Norris. 

On lap 8, a Virtual Safety Car was deployed when Gabriel Bortoleto pulled over at the pit exit with a gearbox issue. With the Brazilian’s stranded Audi threatening a pit lane closure, the field stayed out. That caution proved justified when Gabriel’s brakes caught fire and the pit lane was closed while marshals dealt with the incident. 

When the VSC ended, Charles immediately cut Max’s advantage to 0.7 seconds. Max responded, quickly pulling 1.3 seconds clear again. Further back, Isack was making progress and, by lap 13, had passed Fernando, Cadillac’s Sergio Pérez and Williams’ Alex Albon to rise to P16. 

At the front, GP told Max over the radio that extending his opening stint on Softs would help his race. The Dutchman continued to build his lead over Charles, stretching it to 4.4 seconds.

At the end of lap 18, Hamilton, who had started on Mediums, was the first of the leaders to pit. The Ferrari driver switched to Softs and dropped from P3 to P7. None of his rivals responded, and Max set two more fastest laps on his starting Softs to extend his lead to 6.7 seconds by the start of lap 21. 

Max’s advantage then grew to nine seconds, before second placed Charles stopped on lap 25, fitted Medium tyres and rejoined just ahead of Lewis.

Max Verstappen seals maiden F1 Singapore Grand Prix victory | The Straits Times

# Red Bull’s Max Verstappen coasts to maiden F1 Singapore Grand Prix victory

Deepanraj Ganesan

Published Oct 11, 2026, 09:45 PM

Updated Oct 12, 2026, 10:09 AM

- Max Verstappen won his first Singapore Grand Prix at Marina Bay on Oct 11, after nine previous attempts.
- He converted pole into victory in 1hr 42min 00.785sec, with Charles Leclerc second and Kimi Antonelli third.
- The win was only Verstappen’s second of the 2026 season, while Antonelli’s podium stretched his championship lead to 102 points.

SINGAPORE – Nine appearances, four podiums, three runner-up finishes but not a single victory.

For all his records and success in Formula 1, four-time world champion Max Verstappen had never conquered the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

The narrow track, with its limited overtaking opportunities and gruelling physical demands, had remained an elusive prize for the Dutchman, the third-most successful driver in F1 history by grand prix victories.

When he arrived in Singapore over the weekend, Verstappen knew very clearly that he had “unfinished business” here.

And on Oct 11, at the 10th time of asking, the Red Bull driver finally set that record straight, conquering the streets of Marina Bay to win the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Celebrating his 250th career F1 grand prix weekend in style, Verstappen converted pole to victory in 1hr 42min 00.785sec.

Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc was 7.335sec behind, with Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli third in the 17th edition of the Singapore Grand Prix.

As Verstappen crossed the finishing line after 62 laps, fireworks erupted above the 4.927km track, injecting a much-needed burst of colour into a skyline shrouded in haze over the past week.

The crowd watching the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix at Marina Bay Street Circuit, on Oct 11. ST PHOTO: ARIFFIN JAMAR

Verstappen, 29, said after the win: “It’s taken a while but this race was very good. We had the pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyres and on the medium, even though the medium tyre for everyone was a bit more of a struggle but it worked out, so of course very happy to win here.

“You always try to do your best, luckily it was just good enough. The last few races have been really positive for us, and it’s just great to see. We have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results. It’s a really good group of people. I really enjoy working with them and hopefully we can have a bit more fun till the end of the year.”

After he brought his car to a halt, Verstappen got out of his RB22 and punched the air in delight before leaping into the arms of his jubilant race engineers while the pyrotechnics continued to light up the night sky.

Max Verstappen gets a final handshake moments before he got into his race car for the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix on Oct 11. ST PHOTO: CHONG JUN LIANG

After waiting more than a decade, he had every reason to bask in this glory. The Singapore Grand Prix is one of the few races that the Dutchman had never won previously, despite coming close thrice as he finished second in 2025, 2024 and 2018.

A day before his maiden Grand Prix triumph here, the Dutchman had clinched the 50th pole of his career after winning the first-ever sprint race in Singapore, as he capped a dominant Saturday.

During the main race, Verstappen was barely troubled other than in the opening sequence. While the Dutchman was slow off the line, he managed to squeeze Leclerc to the inside while heading into the first corner and held on to the lead, which he never came close to relinquishing.

The victory in Singapore is Verstappen’s 73rd career win and just his second of the 2026 season. He had clinched his first victory of the campaign at the previous weekend’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Sepang, Malaysia.

Max Verstappen sealed a perfect weekend with victory at the Singapore Grand Prix as Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of clinching the world championship.

The Dutchman won Saturday's sprint from pole and again triumphed from the front of the grid during Sunday's main event under lights, on his 250th Formula 1 Grand Prix start.

The four-time world champion's first victory in Singapore came in dominant fashion, crossing the line 7.3 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc to claim back-to-back wins after his first success of the season in Malaysia last weekend.

It confirmed Red Bull's recent step forward, albeit too late for the 29-year-old to have any hope of halting Antonelli's march to his maiden title.

Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix. Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images

The 20-year-old claimed the final step on the podium at the Marina Bay Circuit, while nearest challenger George Russell recovered to ninth from the back of the grid.

Lewis Hamilton was undone by Ferrari strategy, first angered by being stuck behind teammate Leclerc before failure to pit under the Virtual Safety Car dropped him to sixth. Lando Norris finished fourth ahead of teammate Oscar Piastri.

Antonelli now leads nearest challenger Russell by 102 points with, as things stand, six rounds of the championship remaining.

# Verstappen cruises to first Singapore GP win, Antonelli closes on F1 crown

By Reuters

October 11, 2026 @ 11:02am

Formula One F1 - Singapore Grand Prix - Marina Bay Street Circuit, Singapore - October 11, 2026Red Bull's Max Verstappen celebrates on the podium after winning the Singapore Grand Prix alongside second placed Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and third placed Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli REUTERS/Edgar SuEdgar Su

SINGAPORE: Red Bull's Max Verstappen delivered a commanding performance to win the Singapore Grand Prix from pole position on Sunday, securing his second straight victory of the season after a perfect weekend that included a sprint race triumph.

The Dutchman controlled the race from the start at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, fending off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who finished second while Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was third to close in on a first title.

Verstappen, who won the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, had never won in Singapore before and he had come into the race weekend stating he had "unfinished business."

"It's taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre, even though I think the medium tyre for everyone was more of a struggle," Verstappen said.

"But it worked out, so of course very happy to win here... The last two races have been really positive for us and it's just great to see."

## What To Read Next

Antonelli extended his championship lead over teammate George Russell to 102 points and the Italian can mathematically win the title in the next round in Austin.

"Can I? Really?" a surprised Antonelli said when he was told after his 14th podium of the season.

"Well, let's not worry about that. Let's try to do the best weekend as possible and finish the job."

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had qualified third on the grid but he endured a torrid evening, slipping to sixth behind Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri after the two McLaren drivers overtook him in the dying stages as he struggled with his tyres.

Russell, who started at the back of the grid due to engine penalties, finished ninth behind Liam Lawson and Nico Hulkenberg while Isack Hadjar - who also started at the back - was 10th.

VERSTAPPEN SHUTS THE DOOR

Formula One F1 - Singapore Grand Prix - Marina Bay Street Circuit, Singapore - October 11, 2026Red Bull's Max Verstappen passes the chequered flag to win the Singapore Grand Prix Pool via REUTERS/Ng Han GuanNG HAN GUAN

Leclerc reacted faster than polesitter Verstappen at the start, nearly lining up alongside the Dutchman heading into turn one, but the Red Bull driver veered to the left to shut the door on the Ferrari and retain his lead.

As the race progressed, Verstappen steadily pulled clear on soft tyres, with Red Bull urging him to manage their life as Ferrari threatened an undercut.

Hamilton's struggles became apparent early as he lost pace on medium tyres in third place and Ferrari brought him in for softs before Leclerc pitted on lap 25 in a move timed to emerge ahead of his teammate.

Hamilton's frustration boiled over on team radio as he urged Ferrari to let him past Leclerc, saying: "I need to use this speed, mate," before Leclerc responded by setting the fastest lap.

When Verstappen finally pitted on lap 33, his commanding lead allowed him to rejoin in first place.

Lance Stroll's retirement with clutch issues triggered another VSC period that sparked a flurry of pit stops and Russell's timing proved unfortunate as the VSC ended earlier than expected, dropping him to 10th.

# Verstappen wins Singapore Grand Prix as Antonelli closes in on F1 title 

 By Associated Press - Sunday, October 11, 2026 

SINGAPORE — Silenced by a broken radio, Max Verstappen let his driving do all the talking on the track.

Verstappen raced hard into the first corner then cruised to his second consecutive Formula 1 win at the Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday.

Verstappen had been concerned about his Red Bull car’s “horrendous” starts and was slow off the line again from pole, but managed to squeeze Charles Leclerc to the inside heading into the first corner and held the lead.

Leclerc was second as Verstappen followed up on his first victory of the season in Malaysia last week and sprint race win Saturday. It was his first career Grand Prix win in Singapore at the 10th attempt.

“It’s taken a while,” Verstappen admitted, adding his start was “just good enough.”

After the start, Verstappen’s main concern seemed to be a broken radio that left Red Bull unable to hear him. Race engineer GianPiero Lambiase resorted to asking Verstappen questions he could answer yes or no by pressing his radio transmission button.

Leclerc was second for his first podium finish since July and behind him, there was action as Kimi Antonelli overtook Lando Norris and Lewis Hamilton for third to increase his standings lead.

Antonelli’s Mercedes teammate George Russell came through the field to ninth after starting at the back.

That means Antonelli could now become F1’s youngest-ever champion as soon as the next race, the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas on Oct. 25.

“I know it’s very close. I know it’s there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can,” Antonelli said. “This weekend, I haven’t particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job.”

Once again, Antonelli seemed to have all the luck at Mercedes and Russell none of it.

The Italian was running fifth with Norris and Hamilton ahead when the two British drivers made costly mistakes.

Hamilton ran off track defending from Norris, who seemed startled and also ran wide, allowing Antonelli to line up a pass on Norris before picking off Hamilton a lap later as the seven-time champion struggled with old tires.

The Italian stayed on course despite overheating brakes - “I could even smell it” - and also had to watch out as he was on the verge of a penalty for running off-track too many times, but stayed just the right side of the line from then on.

Russell, meanwhile, was still suffering from his engine failure last week because the need to change his power unit meant a penalty sent him to the back of the grid for the start of Sunday’s race.

Russell was making good progress as he cut through the field to seventh but had a dose of misfortune when a virtual safety car slowdown ended just as he was pitting for fresh tires, leaving him to fight his way back up from 10th.

Norris was fourth for McLaren and his teammate Oscar Piastri passed a struggling Hamilton for fifth on the final lap. Hamilton apologized to the team, saying it had been his decision on the strategy to stay out on wearing tires.

Despite both drivers passing Hamilton late on, it was another race with McLaren well off the pace, though at least without the drama of Norris’ collision with Piastri on Saturday.

Liam Lawson was seventh for Racing Bulls, Nico Hulkenberg eighth for Audi, Russell ninth and Verstappen’s teammate Isack Hadjar recovered to 10th after starting from the pit lane.

Antonelli is on the verge of becoming F1’s youngest champion at the age of 20 and the first Italian to win the title since 1953. He leads Russell by 102 points and Hamilton by 111.

It’s possible that could happen at the Circuit of the Americas on Oct. 25 but highly unlikely.

results.title: Max Verstappen seals perfect weekend with comfortable Singapore Grand Prix win | The Independent
results.author: Scott Hunt
results.text:
Max Verstappen seals perfect weekend with comfortable Singapore Grand Prix win | The Independent

## Kimi Antonelli finished third to lead nearest challenger George Russell by 102 points with six rounds remaining.

Scott Hunt 

Sunday 11 October 2026 15:14 BST

open image in gallery

Max Verstappen won in Singapore for the first time (David Davies/PA) (PA Wire)

Max Verstappen sealed a perfect weekend with victory at the Singapore Grand Prix as Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of clinching the world championship.

The Dutchman won Saturday’s sprint from pole and again triumphed from the front of the grid during Sunday’s main event under lights, on his 250th Formula One Grand Prix start.

The four-time world champion’s first victory in Singapore came in dominant fashion, crossing the line 7.3 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc to claim back-to-back wins after his first success of the season in Malaysia last weekend.

It confirmed Red Bull’s recent step forward, albeit too late for the 29-year-old to have any hope of halting Antonelli’s march to his maiden title.

open image in gallery

Max Verstappen completed a dominant win (David Davies/PA) (PA Wire)

The 20-year-old claimed the final step on the podium at the Marina Bay Circuit, while nearest challenger George Russell recovered to ninth from the back of the grid.

Lewis Hamilton was undone by strategy, first angered by being stuck behind team-mate Leclerc before failure to pit under the virtual safety car dropped him to sixth. Lando Norris finished fourth ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Antonelli now leads nearest challenger Russell by 102 points with, as things stand, six rounds of the championship remaining.

The Italian is now able to secure his place as Formula One’s youngest ever world champion at the Circuit of the Americas in a fortnight – he needs to be 126 points clear following that race.

It also remains a possibility that the penultimate round in Qatar could be cancelled and the season finale in Abu Dhabi replaced by Imola – if F1 bosses decide they cannot race in the Middle East due to the ongoing conflict.

open image in gallery

Kimi Antonelli is closing in on becoming the youngest ever Formula One world champion (David Davies/PA) (PA Wire)

If that happened, 25 available points would be off the table, moving the Italian ever closer to the championship.

Russell’s title challenge to his Mercedes team-mate has firmly hit the buffers over the last week, with a late power-unit failure in Malaysia followed by him crashing into the barriers during Saturday’s sprint here in Singapore.

The 28-year-old also had to start this race from the back of the grid due to an engine change.

Pole-sitter Verstappen fended off a strong start by Leclerc on the run down to turn one, with Hamilton – from third – also having to watch his mirrors for Antonelli.

But the top six remained as they were. Russell moved up to 13th by lap 10.

open image in gallery

Kim Kardashian, girlfriend of Lewis Hamilton, on the grid (David Davies/PA) (PA Wire)

Hamilton was the only frontrunner to start on medium tyres but was the first to pit, on lap 19, to switch to softs.

He remained ahead of Antonelli when the Italian had pitted and Leclerc emerged just ahead of his team-mate when he too had stopped for mediums.

Hamilton was immediately unhappy behind his fellow Ferrari, saying: “We lost two seconds that last lap.” His race engineer responded with: “We saw.”

The radio tussle continued, Hamilton adding “I need to use this speed, mate”, only to be told to manage his tyres.

Lance Stroll broke down to trigger a virtual safety car, under which Leclerc and Antonelli pitted for a cheap stop while Hamilton and Norris did not.

open image in gallery

Lewis Hamilton drives for Ferrari in Singapore (David Davies/PA) (PA Wire)
